references.text: Jesus sends out the twelve with power to heal and proclaim the kingdom of God – this is the mission whose execution verse 6 describes.
Mark's parallel account that the twelve went out, preached repentance, drove out demons, and healed the sick.
Matthew's parallel account where Jesus sends out the twelve with the mission to preach that the kingdom of heaven is near and to heal the sick.
Jesus later sends out the seventy with a similar mission to heal the sick and proclaim that the kingdom of God has come near – a parallel sending.
The apostles continued in the temple and in homes to teach and proclaim the gospel about Christ – a continuation of the same mission to preach and heal.
Jesus himself preached the gospel of the kingdom of God in the synagogues from village to village, which the disciples now do in his footsteps.
Jesus traveled throughout Galilee, preaching in the synagogues and driving out demons – the disciples' ministry in verse 6 mirrors Jesus' own work.
Those who were scattered after the persecution in Jerusalem went about preaching the gospel, and Philip preached Christ in Samaria – a similar pattern of traveling from place to place and preaching.
Jesus traveled from city to city and from village to village, preaching the gospel of the kingdom of God – the disciples now carry out the same mission.
